name: adp-observability skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the adp-observability skill adds value over the published Agentic Data Plane docs (https://docs.redpanda.com/agentic-data-plane/) and the rpk ai command reference the Docs MCP serves. Fact cases were picked from the full skill before its thin conversion, without checking the published docs: sampled at even intervals through references/observability.md (traces, transcripts, the audit log) and targeted at claims expected to be missing from the docs. The behavioral cases grade the outcome of a task run against a mocked rpk ai: naming every server a grouped, partly denied audit log call refused; finding a conversation by what was said, which --query does not search; and listing conversations that completed after a failed tool call.

test_cases.query: In the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane Traces view, one of our agent runs had a tool call fail, then the agent retried with a different tool and gave the user a correct answer. What status does that trace show in the list? And from the terminal, how would I list the last day's runs that had a failed tool call in them, including ones like this that recovered?
test_cases.why: A trace's status is Error only when the run itself failed. A run that finished with a failed tool call inside it reads Completed, with the failed-call count beside the status. `rpk ai trace list --errors` covers failed runs and runs with a failed tool call, which `--status error` does not. A model would guess the trace shows Error.
verified_against: product source (trace status ERROR only when the run itself failed; failed tool call count; rpk ai trace list --errors help)

invariants.name: completed_not_error
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the trace shows Error (or Failed) status, or gives only `--status error` as the way to find such runs. PASSES if it says the trace shows Completed (optionally noting a failed-call count beside it) and lists such runs with `rpk ai trace list` using `--errors` and a one-day window such as `--since 24h`.

test_cases.query: In the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane Traces view I picked 25 users in the User filter, and now the list seems to show traces from every user, including ones I didn't pick. When I picked 10 users it worked. What's going on?
test_cases.why: Each Traces filter facet takes at most 20 values. Past that the UI drops the facet's filter silently instead of reporting an error, so the list goes unfiltered. Only visible in the UI source.
verified_against: product source (Traces view search schema: at most 20 values per facet, an over-long list falls back to no filter)

invariants.name: twenty_value_cap_silent
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer blames caching, permissions, or a bug without naming the value limit, or names a limit other than 20. PASSES if it says a filter facet accepts at most 20 values and that past that the filter stops applying without an error, so the user should pick 20 or fewer (or split the search).

test_cases.query: A teammate opening a trace in the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane sees some spans marked Restricted. Can they still see anything about those spans, and which permission would let them read the content?
test_cases.why: A restricted span keeps its shape visible: kind, timing, token use, the emitting agent, error code and gateway status. Prompts, messages and tool payloads stay hidden. The content needs dataplane_adp_trace_content_read, or for an agent's spans transcript read on that agent. A model would guess the whole span is hidden.
verified_against: product source (trace API: redacted span fields; GetTrace redaction rules; trace permissions)

invariants.name: shape_visible_content_hidden
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says nothing about a restricted span is visible, or names no trace content permission. PASSES if it says the span still shows metadata such as its kind, timing or token usage (any two of kind, timing, tokens, agent, error code) while prompts, messages or tool payloads are hidden, and names the trace content-read permission (dataplane_adp_trace_content_read or Trace.read_content). Also mentioning transcript read access on the agent is fine.

test_cases.query: `rpk ai agent transcript list support --tool-errors-only --since 30d` returns a handful of recent conversations, but none from earlier in the month, even though when I open one of those older conversations with `rpk ai agent transcript get` it clearly shows a failed tool call. Why doesn't the filter find it?
test_cases.why: The list filter reads a stored per-conversation count of failed tool calls. A conversation last written before that count existed reads zero until new activity republishes it, while `get` derives the count from the conversation's own tool calls. Only visible in the storage source.
verified_against: product source (transcript list storage: rows written before the failed tool call count column existed count as 0)

invariants.name: stored_count_missing_on_older
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer blames the --since window, a permission, a retention limit, or says the filter is working and the tool call did not really fail, without naming the stored count. PASSES if it says the filter reads a per-conversation failed-tool-call count that conversations written before the count was introduced do not have (they read as zero until updated), while get computes it from the tool calls, so older conversations must be opened to see their tool errors.

test_cases.query: I'm reading `rpk ai agent transcript get support <conversation-id>` to check exactly what a tool returned, but the tool output stops partway through. Did ADP only store part of the result? How do I see all of it?
test_cases.why: The table and wide views of `transcript get` truncate tool input and output to 500 characters for readability. `-o json` and `-o yaml` return the full, untruncated structure. The help text does not say so.
verified_against: product source (rpk ai agent transcript get: truncate(..., 500) in the readable log)

invariants.name: display_truncation
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says ADP stored only part of the result, or that the full output cannot be retrieved. PASSES if it says the readable (table) view truncates tool input and output and that -o json or -o yaml shows the full payload. Naming the 500-character limit is not required.

test_cases.query: One of our Redpanda Agentic Data Plane agent conversations has been running on and off for about a month. If its transcript's error notice lists no errors, can I conclude nothing failed in that conversation since it started?
test_cases.why: A transcript's recorded-error list covers at most the seven days before the conversation's last turn, up to 1,000 records; past either limit the notice says the history is limited, and a failed lookup reports the records unavailable. A model would treat an empty list as proof.
verified_against: product source (transcript API: errors snapshot covers at most seven days before the latest turn, at most 1000 records, errors_truncated and errors_unavailable)

invariants.name: bounded_window
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says yes, an empty error list proves nothing failed, or gives a window other than seven days. PASSES if it says no, because the error records cover only the seven days before the last turn (and at most 1,000 records), so older failures can be missing; it may suggest reading the turns and tool calls.

test_cases.query: In a Redpanda Agentic Data Plane transcript's Detailed view, one turn's context chip says about 41k tokens, but the same turn's input tokens add up to about 120k. Is one of those numbers wrong?
test_cases.why: Neither is wrong. The context size is the prompt the model read on the turn's last model call, cache reads included; the input-token total sums every model call in the turn and is what it cost. A multi-call turn reports a context size smaller than its input total.
verified_against: product source (transcript turn context_tokens: the last LLM step's input; usage.input_tokens summed across every step)

invariants.name: last_call_vs_sum
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says one number is wrong or a bug, or explains the gap only by caching or compaction without saying the input total sums several model calls. PASSES if it says the context chip is the prompt size of the turn's last model call while the input-token total adds up every model call in the turn, so with several calls the total is larger.

test_cases.query: A Redpanda Agentic Data Plane transcript shows a 'Context compacted' marker with a before size of 180k tokens and an after size of 60k. Our model provider's bill for that turn doesn't match either number. Which should I trust for cost?
test_cases.why: Compaction sizes are the agent's own heuristic estimates of the request it was about to send, not billed usage, so they do not reconcile with the turn's token totals. Use the token totals or Cost and usage for spend.
verified_against: product source (transcript API: compaction context sizes are the agent SDK's heuristic estimates, not billed usage)

invariants.name: estimates_not_billing
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the compaction sizes are billed tokens or should match the bill. PASSES if it says the before and after sizes are the agent's estimates of the request size, not billed usage, and points to the turn's recorded token usage or the cost and usage view for spend.

test_cases.query: In the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane audit log, an MCP tool call by our support agent shows Outcome Denied, yet the access policy grants that agent the tool and other calls to the same tool show Allowed. How can that be, and where in the audit log do I confirm what refused it?
test_cases.why: Denied covers a refusal by access policy and a call that was authorized and then blocked by a guardrail or data policy. The event's details list the checks in order: an Access row of Permit and a Guardrail (or Data policy) row of Blocked shows the later check stopped it.
verified_against: product source (audit log API: DENIED means refused by authorization or authorized then withheld by a guardrail; policy decisions PERMIT, DENY, BLOCK, MASK)

invariants.name: guardrail_after_access
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer blames only the access policy (a missing grant, caching, or a stale policy) and never mentions a guardrail or data policy. PASSES if it says a guardrail or data policy that runs after access is granted can block the call and still record Denied, and says to open the event and read its policy decisions (access permitted, guardrail or data policy blocked).

test_cases.query: In the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane audit log, a large share of events show an actor type of Unknown. Are those calls from unauthenticated or anonymous callers that we should worry about?
test_cases.why: Actor type is empty, shown as Unknown, on events recorded before the field existed and on configuration changes, which carry no account type. It means the type was not recorded, not that the caller was anonymous.
verified_against: product source (audit log API: actor_type empty on events emitted before the field existed and on entity management events; treat empty as unknown)

invariants.name: unknown_means_not_recorded
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says Unknown means unauthenticated or anonymous callers, or treats them as a security concern without naming why the type is missing. PASSES if it says Unknown means the actor type was not recorded, because the event is older than the field or is a configuration change, which records no account type.

test_cases.query: I want to count how many MCP sessions clients opened against our Redpanda Agentic Data Plane MCP gateway last week. Can I count the `initialize` entries in the audit log to get that?
test_cases.why: The MCP gateway audits session setup and upkeep (initialize, ping, tools/list, notifications) only when refused or failed; tool calls are always recorded. Counting initialize entries counts failed or refused handshakes, not sessions.
verified_against: product source (AI Gateway MCP audit hook: handshake and session upkeep audited only when refused or failed)

invariants.name: initialize_only_on_failure
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says yes, counting initialize entries gives the session count. PASSES if it says no, because initialize (and other setup messages such as ping or tools/list) is recorded only when refused or failed, so successful sessions leave no initialize entry.

test_cases.query: An MCP client connected to our Redpanda Agentic Data Plane gateway, listed the tools, and then disconnected without calling any tool. I can't find any trace for it in the Traces view. Does that mean the connection never reached the gateway?
test_cases.why: Traces lists gateway traces only when they hold a model call or a tool call. Session setup, tool discovery and keepalives alone produce no listed trace, so its absence is not proof the client never connected.
verified_against: product source (trace list storage: a gateway trace is listed only with a customer-facing span, an LLM call or MCP tool call)

invariants.name: upkeep_not_traced
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the missing trace means the connection failed or never reached the gateway. PASSES if it says a session that only set up and listed tools produces no trace, because traces show runs with a model or tool call, so the absence does not mean the connection failed.

test_cases.query: In the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane Traces view, what's the difference between a trace marked Running and one marked Incomplete? When does one become the other?
test_cases.why: Running means the root span is still open, or there is no root span and spans arrived in the last 15 minutes. Incomplete means no root span and no span in the last 15 minutes, so the record is partial. A gateway-only trace is never either.
verified_against: product source (trace API: TraceStatus RUNNING and INCOMPLETE definitions)

invariants.name: root_span_and_15_minutes
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer gives a different time threshold or does not tie the difference to a missing root span. PASSES if it says Incomplete is a trace with no root span and no new span for 15 minutes, while Running means the root span is still open or spans arrived within the last 15 minutes.

test_cases.query: Bob (bob@acme.com) says the MCP servers page in our Redpanda Agentic Data Plane console showed him only some of our servers this morning. Use the audit log to find out exactly which servers he was refused and which policy refused them. You can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: The page load is one ListMCPServers call that decided on eight servers, so the audit log shows it as one grouped row with outcome partial and no single resource. `--outcome denied` alone misses it. `rpk ai auditlog get` on the row reads one member event, never the group, so it names one server at most. The members, one row per server, come from `rpk ai auditlog list --correlation-id <id>` (or a list that asks for the resources field). Graded on the outcome: the answer names all three refused servers and the deciding policy, however the agent got them.
verified_against: product source (rpk ai auditlog list and get help; audit log API: partial outcome, resource_count, resources is a list-view field that GetAuditLogEntry never fills, correlation_id expansion)

mock.name: run_shell
mock.description: Run a shell command on the user's workstation and return its combined stdout and stderr. rpk is installed with the rpk ai plugin, signed in to the user's Agentic Data Plane, with an environment selected. Commands run non-interactively.

command.description: The shell command line to run, for example: rpk ai agent list

responses.output:
Search the ADP audit log: who did what, to which resource, and which policy
allowed or denied it. One row is one API call. A call that decided on several
resources is one grouped row; RESOURCE_COUNT says how many.

--since defaults to 24h, or to no lower bound with --correlation-id. It takes
an RFC 3339 timestamp, a duration ago (15m, 24h, 7d, 2w), or "all" for no lower
bound. "all" scans the whole archive and can run into the server's 30s query
limit. --until must be after --since.

Filter flags (--actor, --resource-type, --policy, ...) each match one field:
  - values within one flag are ORed; different flags are ANDed
  - repeat a flag or separate values with commas; a literal comma is \,
  - a leading ! negates: --subsystem '!llm-proxy'; a literal leading ! is \!
  - the resource, parent, --policy and --status flags match a call when any
    one of its resources matches, and return the whole call

--denied is shorthand for --outcome denied,partial: anything with a refusal
in it. --outcome denied alone leaves out partly denied calls.

-o table shows a lean column set; -o wide, json, yaml and markdown add the
decision and delegation fields. --fields picks the fields (and the table
columns); --fields all returns every field, including the request and entity
bodies, which is slower. 'rpk ai auditlog get ID' reads one entry in full.

--limit caps the entries printed (default 50; 0 returns everything). When more
remain, the exit code stays 0 and stderr gets the flags that continue the
listing. When nothing matches, stderr names the filter that was sent.

Reading the audit log is itself audited; --operation '!ListAuditLogEntries'
hides those reads.

Usage:
  rpk ai auditlog list [flags]

Flags:
      --activity strings         activity: create, read, update, delete
      --actor strings            effective user email (the human on a delegated call)
      --actor-type strings       actor kind: user, agent, service-account
      --agent strings            agent name; a bare name also matches agents/<name>
      --correlation-id string    one call's member events, one row per resource, denials first; any age unless --since is set
      --denied                   only calls with a refusal in them (outcome denied or partial)
      --event-class strings      event class: api-activity, entity-management (config changes)
      --fields strings           fields to return, also the table columns (comma-separated), or "all"
      --limit int                maximum entries to print; 0 returns everything (default 50)
      --operation strings        operation: CreateLLMProvider, tools/call, chat/completions, ...
      --order-by string          sort field with an optional " desc" (default "time desc")
      --outcome strings          call verdict: allowed, denied, partial, masked (repeatable, comma-separated)
      --page-token string        resume a previous listing from the token it wrote to stderr
      --policy strings           any policy the decision was attributed to
      --query string             case-insensitive substring of the entry message
      --resource-id strings      resource id
      --resource-type strings    resource type as a CLI noun: mcp-server, llm-provider, agent, ...
      --since string             start of the window (default "24h")
      --status strings           operation status: succeeded, failed (the verdict is --outcome)
      --subsystem strings        product surface: llm-proxy, mcp-gateway, a2a-proxy, agents, guardrails, ...
      --until string             end of the window, exclusive and after --since

Global Flags:
  -o, --output string   output format: table, wide, json, yaml, markdown (default "table")

Read one audit log entry with every field, including the request and entity
bodies that list leaves out. -o yaml is the readable form for those. --fields
narrows the entry to the named fields.

get reads one event, not a grouped call, so its resources field is never
filled. When a list row shows a resource_count above 1, the call's members come
from 'rpk ai auditlog list --correlation-id <correlation_id>', one row per
resource; each member's id works with get.

Usage:
  rpk ai auditlog get <id> [flags]

Flags:
      --fields strings   fields to return (comma-separated); default all

Global Flags:
  -o, --output string   output format: table, wide, json, yaml, markdown (default "table")

Read the ADP audit log (read-only).

Usage:
  rpk ai auditlog [command]

Aliases:
  auditlog, audit-log, audit

Available Commands:
  get         Read one audit log entry
  list        Search the audit log
  query       Query audit entries, timeline and facets (set a bounded time window)

Manage access policies.

Usage:
  rpk ai policy [command]

Available Commands:
  get, list, create, update, delete

Usage:
  rpk ai [command]

Available Commands:
  agent, agent-network, auditlog, auth, env, gateway, mcp-server, model, policy, provider, session, spending, trace, trigger

Use "rpk ai [command] --help" for more information about a command.
